names.name: the unmanifest (avyakta), knower of the field

descriptions: The supreme self is changeless, eternal, the seer, cause of consciousness together with mind, the elements' qualities and the senses (Ca Sū 1.56).
Disengagement is release: the supreme, tranquil, imperishable — that is brahman, that is liberation (Ca Śā 5.11); sinless, passionless, deathless, brahman, nirvāṇa (5.23).
The person is the measure of the world: brahman is the inner self (Śā 5.4-5).
negations: The self become brahman is not perceived and has no mark (Ca Śā 1.155).
'This is not I, this is not mine' (Ca Śā 1.153).
relation_to_self: The individual self is eternal, beginningless and (for Caraka) all-pervading; the empirical person is the aggregate born of delusion, desire, aversion and karma; release is that self 'become brahman'.
relation_to_world: The world is real and made of the five elements; the person and the world correspond member for member; seeing oneself in all and all in oneself gives rise to the true understanding.
caveat: Āyurveda is a science of life rather than a soteriology: its purpose is health (Ca Sū 30.26), and its metaphysics (chiefly Caraka Śā 1 and 5, Suśruta Śā 1) is close to Sāṃkhya-Yoga and Vaiśeṣika. No creator is required — Kāṅkāyana's Prajāpati-theory is rejected in Ca Sū 25, and Suśruta leaves the 'source' open among nature, the Lord, time, chance, destiny and transformation (Su Śā 1.11); Caraka and Suśruta differ on whether selves are all-pervading. It would reject any reading that makes medicine itself the means of liberation, while holding health to be the root of all four aims.

names.name: the conscious light (cinmaya jyotis), supreme bliss

descriptions: Liberation in life is knowledge of identity with Śiva in an ageless, deathless body (Rasārṇava 1.8).

The conscious light between the brows: supreme bliss, of the nature of light, free of conception, peaceful, self-known; seeing the whole world as consciousness one attains brahmanhood here (Rasahṛdaya 1.21-23; SDS 46-48).
Mercury is Śiva's own seed and is praised as equal to the supreme brahman (Rasārṇava 1.36; SDS 49-51).
negations: Free of conception (avikalpa), free of all afflictions (Rasahṛdaya 1.22).
relation_to_self: The Raseśvaras are Māheśvaras who hold identity (tādātmya) with the Supreme Lord; the self realizes it only in a stable body.
relation_to_world: The world is to be seen as consciousness; mercury and mica, seeds of Śiva and the Goddess, make the divine body.
caveat: The tradition would reject any one-truth reading that allows liberation without the stable, undecaying body ('liberation after the body falls is meaningless'). Its practices are restricted and are recorded here only in summary.
